title: The outfit, then the work that pays for it
summary: Show off a full outfit, then cut to the real, everyday work that pays for it. AI plans the shots, the cut and the overlay text.
why: A TikTok trends roundup updated October 26, 2026 lists outfit and work reveals set to a new pop single called "Housewife": creators show their look, then the job that pays for it. A UGC trend report for October 17 to 24 also lists the song under lifestyle montages.
steps: Use the main prompt to plan the two halves: the outfit reveal and the work clip.
Film the outfit like a mini runway: feet first, a slow tilt up, a turn.
Film 2 or 3 short clips of your real work, the messier and more honest the better.
Cut on a beat from the last outfit pose straight into the work, and add the overlay text. Pick a trending sound in the app so the audio is licensed.

prompts.label: Main prompt
prompts.text: I'm making a short vertical video in two halves: first my best outfit, then the real work that pays for it. My job is [your job or side hustle]. Write: 1) a shot list for a 6-second outfit reveal I can film alone with my phone on a shelf; 2) three quick work clips that honestly show what my day looks like; 3) the exact moment to cut between the two; 4) five options for funny, self-aware overlay text, under 12 words each. No brand names.

prompts.label: Variation: ordinary jobs
prompts.text: Write 10 overlay text ideas for an "outfit, then the work that pays for it" video, one for each of these jobs: nurse on night shift, snowplough driver, teacher, barista, plumber, student with a part-time job, farmer, warehouse worker, parent at home with toddlers, retail worker in holiday season. Keep them warm and funny, never mean about any job.

prompts.label: Variation: small business
prompts.text: I run a [type of small business]. Plan a 10-second video: first me dressed up for a night out, then the behind-the-scenes work that keeps the business going (packing orders, early mornings, cleaning up). Give me a shot list, the cut point, and 4 overlay lines that are honest and a bit funny. Don't make up sales numbers or customer quotes.

tips: The contrast is the joke. The dressier the outfit and the more ordinary the work, the better it lands.
Keep the work clips real. Viewers love seeing the unglamorous part.
Use the app's own trending sound so you don't run into music rights problems.
Don't show customers, patients, students or coworkers without asking them first, and never film private details at work.
